objective: At n = 2^m >= 8 prove that the contact (n + 2, n + 3) of the doubled box [0, 2n - 2]^2 never reads either contact of the corner ring (0, 0), so full reach fails; equivalently (to be proved) that on the grid [0, n - 2] x [0, n - 1] whose walker moves to a 4-neighbour except leftwards on the bottom row and rightwards on the top row, the walks of every length from (0, 0) to (n/2 + 1, n/2 + 1) are even in number. Secondary targets: the corner return law (the generating function of the corner's returns is 1/(1 + L(w^4)), L the trace polynomial of GF(2n)) and the exact failing set (n - 4 contacts, each missing exactly the three rings of one corner). Found before registration, by computation: all three at sides 8 to 32 (the failing set to 64).
status: Proved 2026-11-10 (by hand, with finite checks, refereed; pre-registered in 03bd5937b): the failure at n follows from one walk count, (1, 0) never reading d* = (n + 3, n + 2), which on the h contacts is an even count of conveyor-grid walks from (0, 0) to (n/2 + 1, n/2 + 1); the reflection in X - Y = 1 is a symmetry of the walk, and mod 2 only excursions above the diagonal that touch the left or top wall survive; the strip at a power of two has, besides lambda = 0, the single branch lambda = t + 1/t with decaying root w^2 C(w^4); a conservation law for anti-diagonal sums. Computed: the count vanishes and the failure holds at every power of two from 8 to 128; the corner return law 1/(1 + L(w^4)), L the trace polynomial of GF(2n), at 4 to 128. The registered target, the failure at every power of two, is not proved.
title: The failure at every power of two
